knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The spot test on an unnoticeable area comes before any product touches the stain. Spraying straight onto the stain, or mixing products, skips the test and risks damage.
Working from the outside edge toward the centre stops the stain spreading. Working from the centre outward, or at random, moves the stain across the surface.
A changed test area and a stain that has not responded to repeats mean the treatment must stop. The learner records the outcome and refers it. A stronger product or hot water risks further damage.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied stain sample and a supplied surface, the learner identifies the stain type and the surface or material, and states which products are on the approved list, observed by the assessor.

The learner performs a spot test with the approved product on a marked, unnoticeable area, waits the contact time, and reports the test result. Pass condition: the assessor observes the test before the product is used on the stain.

The learner removes solids and liquid by the approved method, applies the approved product to the stain, and works from the outside toward the centre with a small brush. Pass condition: the assessor observes the direction of work.

The learner rinses the surface with water and blots it dry with a white cloth or white paper towel, then checks whether the stain is gone. Pass condition: the learner repeats once, and refers the stain if it remains.

The learner completes the stain record for the supplied stain, with the location, surface, stain type, product and dilution, test result and outcome. Pass condition: the record matches what the assessor observed.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Completed stain record for the supplied stain
Before and after photograph of the test area and the treated stain
stopWorkCriteria: Learner applies a product to the stain without a spot test
Learner uses a product that is not approved for the surface, or mixes two products
Learner uses a solvent-based product on a synthetic material without checking the material first
Learner continues after the test area changes colour, texture or shows damage
Learner adds more product, or a stronger product, after a treatment has had no effect
Learner works without gloves while a stain remover is in use
